record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: For the Drop-The-Larger-Hopeless policy in deadline-based scheduling, what is the probability that an arriving job is dropped?

evidence.quote: Understanding the dropping probability under DTLH is also an open problem, although the dropping probability for DIH is understood, under certain conditions; see [76].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with the following setup. Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$. Each arriving job $i$ has an i.i.d. service-time requirement $S_i$ drawn from a known distribution and an i.i.d. relative deadline $D_i$ drawn from a known distribution; the job must complete service by time $A_i + D_i$, where $A_i$ is its arrival time. At any time $t$, a job currently in the system is called "hopeless" if, given its remaining service requirement and the current system state, it cannot possibly meet its deadline (for instance, under any non-preemptive or preemptive work-conserving schedule its deadline will be missed with certainty).

The Drop-The-Larger-Hopeless (DTLH) admission/scheduling policy is defined as follows. Upon each arrival, and whenever the set of hopeless jobs in the system changes, the policy identifies all hopeless jobs currently present (including possibly the new arrival). If the set of hopeless jobs is nonempty, the policy drops the hopeless job with the largest (remaining) service requirement. The server otherwise serves jobs according to a deadline-aware discipline (e.g., earliest-deadline-first among non-hopeless jobs).

Determine, in closed form or as a tractable expression, the steady-state probability $p_{\mathrm{drop}}$ that an arbitrary arriving job is eventually dropped under the DTLH policy, as a function of $\lambda$ and the distributions of $S$ and $D$.
artifact.status_search_result: The dropping probability under the Drop-The-Larger-Hopeless (DTLH) policy is explicitly listed as an open problem in the surveyed literature on queueing theory motivated by datacenter computing. Web search did not surface any analysis resolving the DTLH dropping probability; the related Drop-the-Inevitably-Hopeless (DIH) policy has been analyzed under certain conditions, but no analogous result for DTLH was found.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Routing and Scheduling of Customers with Deadlines
status_evidence.snippet: Studies deadline scheduling but does not analyze DTLH dropping probability.
status_evidence.claim: No analysis of the DTLH dropping probability is provided in known deadline-scheduling literature.

status_evidence.title: Maximizing Service Reward for Queues with Deadlines
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses deadline-aware queueing rewards; does not derive DTLH dropping probability.
status_evidence.claim: The DTLH dropping probability remains unaddressed in available queueing-with-deadlines papers.
